name: quant_int8
summary: per-row symmetric int8 quantization of an R x C f32 matrix: s[r] = max_c |x[r][c]| / 127 (f32), q[r][c] = clamp(round_half_even(x[r][c] / s[r]), -127, 127) (i8); a zero row gives s = 0 and q = 0
provenance: authored for OpenAccel Lab (Apache-2.0); the per-row absmax scheme of LLM.int8()-style weight quantization

q.why: the reference is round_half_even(127 x / amax) on the exact values (numpy rint in float64). An entrant divides by its own f32 scale s' = (amax/127)(1+e1) and rounds y' = (x/s')(1+e2), |e1|, |e2| <= 5u (2.5 ulp, the OpenCL C single-precision divide limit without -cl-fp32-correctly-rounded-divide-sqrt; 1 ulp <= 2u relative), so |y' - y| <= |y|((1+5u)/(1-5u)^2 - 1) with |y| <= 127: WolframLanguageEvaluator: u=2^-24; N[127*((1+5u)/(1-5u)^2-1),10] -> 0.0001135469047. That is < 1/2, so the two roundings differ by at most 1 (only when y is within 1.2e-4 of a half-integer). A wrong scale (no abs, wrong divisor) or a sign error moves q by far more than 1.

s.why: amax is exact (abs and max do not round); s = amax/127 is one division, correctly rounded on IEEE hosts and within 2.5 ulp under OpenCL C (s7.4) and Triton's GPU fdiv. 1 ulp <= 2u relative, so 2.5 ulp <= 5u: WolframLanguageEvaluator: u=2^-24; N[(5/2)*2^-23/u] -> 5.; N[5u,10] -> 2.980232239*10^-7.
